core_obligations: Record what has to be proved: with p_i the projections, t_i and t'_i the images of t and t' and xi_i the image of xi, the relative assassin condition at xi_i is automatic by base change of the relative assassin, so only the emptiness of the closure of xi_i intersected with the fibre over t_i has to be shown for some i (proof lines 4582-4589).

First proof: let Z_i and Z be the closures of xi_i and xi with reduced induced structure, use that Z is the limit of the Z_i, choose a field k mapping to t and observe that Z times_T Spec(k) is the limit of the quasi-compact pieces Z_i times_{T_i} Spec(k) because limits commute with fibred products; since the limit is empty, one of those quasi-compact pieces is empty, and its image of Spec(k) in T_i is t_i (proof lines 4591-4610).

Second proof: apply the separation lemma to Z to obtain an open neighbourhood V of t, a locally finitely presented morphism T' -> S, a diagram and a closed subscheme Z' of X_{T'} disjoint from the fibre of Z' over a(t) and containing the image of Z over V; take V affine, descend it to an affine open V_i of a stage, use the characterisation of locally finitely presented morphisms to factor the restriction of a through a morphism from V_i to T' after increasing i, and conclude that the induced morphism sends xi_i into Z', so the closure of xi_i misses the fibre over t_i (proof lines 4612-4641).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the single emptiness statement using base change of the relative assassin (proof lines 4582-4589).
First proof: write the nonempty fibre product over the closed point as a limit of quasi-compact pieces and use emptiness of the limit (proof lines 4591-4610).
Second proof: separate the closed set from the fibre by a locally finitely presented model and descend that model to a stage (proof lines 4612-4641).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that an impurity of a module above a point, presented over a directed limit of affine schemes, already appears at some finite stage of the system (statement lines 4572-4580, tag 05IZ). The proof reduces to a single emptiness assertion after observing that the associated point condition transports by base change, and then gives two genuinely different arguments: the first writes the (empty) fibre product of the closure with the residue field as a filtered limit of quasi-compact pieces so that one piece must be empty, and the second separates the closed set from the special fibre by a locally finitely presented replacement morphism and descends that replacement, together with an affine open neighbourhood, to a stage of the system. The descent of the replacement morphism is the substance, so the claim is H2.
